thread.title: Dow Dives 600 Points, Breaks Key Support; Fear Gauge Spikes Again

author: KEN SHREVE
title: Dow Dives 600 Points, Breaks Key Support; Fear Gauge Spikes Again
text:
The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq composite briefly fought back early Monday from sharp opening losses, but bears regained control in afternoon trading, sending the major averages to session lows.
X The Dow Jones industrial average lagged, falling 2.5%, or more than 600 points, undercutting its 50-day moving average.
The Dow was hurt by more weakness in Exxon Mobil ( XOM ). Shares fell another 5% on the heels of Friday's 5% drop. The oil giant gave up longer-term support at the 200-day moving average.
Technology names in the Dow held up well, with stocks like Cisco Systems ( CSCO ), Apple ( AAPL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Intel ( INTC ) showing modest gains or losses.
Goldman Sachs ( GS ) slid 2% in the Dow. Financials were generally weak after the Federal Reserved levied sanctions against Wells Fargo ( WFC ) on Friday, citing "widespread consumer abuses and compliance breakdowns." Shares of Wells Fargo slumped around 9%. JPMorgan ( JPM ) gave back 2%.
The S&P 500 was down 2.2%, also below its 50-day line, and the Nasdaq composite dropped 1.8%. Volume on the NYSE and Nasdaq was tracking close to Friday's levels in the stock market today .
The Russell 2000 small-cap index and broad-based NYSE composite showed notable price action as both gave up support at the 50-day moving average. The Russell 2000 was down 1.7% while the NYSE Composite fell 2.2%.
Meanwhile, a popular fear gauge hit its highest level since November 2016. After soaring about 30% Friday, the Cboe Volatility Index jumped 47% Monday.
Nvidia ( NVDA ) lagged in the Nasdaq 100, falling more than 4%, but technical damage has been limited so far. It's still holding above a 218.77 buy point and the 50-day moving average. Earnings are due Thursday after the close.
Qualcomm ( QCOM ) gave back nearly 5% even as Broadcom ( AVGO ) raised its bid for the chipmaker by 17% to $82 a share, calling the deal its "best and final offer."
Inside the IBD 50 , Casa Systems ( CASA ) was a bright spot. Shares jumped shot up as high as 22.50 briefly clearing an IPO base with a 21.39 buy point. But shares pared gains to 1.4% at 20.90.
Elsewhere in the IBD 50, China-based Sina ( SINA ) and Leaderboard name SVB Financial ( SIVB ) fell 3% each. Both are close to tests of the 50-day moving average, along with other IBD 50 names like IPG Photonics ( IPGP ) and Alibaba ( BABA ).
